model_annotation: The chart displays the percentage of employment rates across different age groups, categorized by migration background and history. The x-axis represents age, ranging from 20 to 75 years in increments of 5, while the y-axis denotes the employment rate as a percentage, spanning from 0% to 100% in increments of 20%. The chart features four distinct lines, each representing a specific category: individuals without a migration background (black, solid line), those who migrated before 2009 (grey, solid line), individuals with a migration background (light blue, solid line), and those who immigrated to Germany since 2010 and were born in Germany (dark blue, solid line). The black line starts at approximately 55% at age 25 and rises to a peak of around 60% between ages 40 and 50 before gradually declining to about 15% at age 75. The grey line follows a similar pattern, beginning at roughly 45% at age 25, peaking at approximately 55% between ages 40 and 50, and then decreasing to around 10% at age 75. The light blue line commences at about 40% at age 25, reaches a maximum of around 50% between ages 35 and 45, and subsequently drops to approximately 5% at age 75. The dark blue line begins at roughly 15% at age 30, experiences fluctuations before rising to a peak of around 20% at age 60, and then declines to about 5% at age 75, with a notable spike to approximately 25% at age 70.
